findings.summary: The comment claims the sentinel covers the case where the target 'rejected the pack outright', but a genuine 413 body-limit rejection can never reach it: `subdivide` is true and the relaxed-retry block requires `abortedEarly`, so `relaxedRetried` stays false and the gate at line 686 is skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: Confirmed by probe: a 1-commit chain whose PushPack returns `http 413: body exceeded size limit 1000` returns the plain retryable `push bootstrap batch for refs/heads/main: http 413: ...` — no sentinel — after 1 push. A repo whose first checkpoint push gets a hard 413 with no prior self-imposed abort therefore stays in the redelivery loop forever, which is the failure mode the PR exists to end. The sentinel only ever fires after a self-imposed abort has already happened.

findings.short_summary: Relaxed budget leaks to later checkpoints and branches
findings.summary: `selfImposedBudget = p.AnnouncedTargetLimit` mutates a variable declared at function scope (line 366) and never restores it, so the raised ceiling leaks to every later checkpoint and every later branch in the run.
findings.failure_scenario: Target announces 10 GiB; TargetMaxPack is 512 MiB. Checkpoint 7 bottoms out, is retried at 10 GiB, and succeeds. For checkpoints 8..N and for every subsequent branch the abort ceiling is now 10 GiB while the pre-flight estimate still plans against p.TargetMaxPack (512 MiB) — a pack the estimate calls 400 MiB but which is really 4 GiB now uploads in full instead of aborting at ~486 MiB. That breaks the 'bounds the waste of a doomed push' invariant the PR claims to keep ('Doesn't raise the batching budget'). It also silently disables the fix for branch 2+: `relaxedRetried` is reset per branch but the budget is not, so `p.AnnouncedTargetLimit > selfImposedBudget` is then false — no retry, and no permanent classification either.

findings.short_summary: isIndivisibleCheckpoint measures wrong gap on resume path
findings.summary: `isIndivisibleCheckpoint` derives `prev` from `batch.Checkpoints[idx-1]` instead of the loop's `current`, so it measures the wrong gap on the stale-temp-ref re-plan path where startIdx is reset to 0 while `current` holds a non-zero ResumeHash.
findings.failure_scenario: executeBatched lines 397-413 replace `batch.Checkpoints` with `evenCheckpoints(remaining, ...)` and set `startIdx = 0` while `current = batch.ResumeHash`. At idx 0, isIndivisibleCheckpoint uses `prev = plumbing.ZeroHash`, so subdivideCheckpoints sees `curIdx = -1` and a gap of `cpIdx+1` counted from the chain root rather than from ResumeHash — it reports 'divisible' for a checkpoint that subdivideToFactor just proved indivisible. Result: after the relaxed retry has already fired and failed, the run returns a plain retryable error instead of the sentinel — on exactly the resume route this PR series (ENT-2054) exists for. Pass `current` in instead.

findings.short_summary: Parsed in-loop 413 limit never feeds AnnouncedTargetLimit
findings.summary: The batch loop parses `parsedLimit := targetBodyLimit(pushErr)` on every rejection but never feeds it into `p.AnnouncedTargetLimit`; the field is populated only on Execute's one-shot auto-switch path (line 232), so whole configurations can never reach the relaxed retry.
findings.failure_scenario: With `--target-max-pack-bytes` set (or once the GitHub large-repo preflight at line 1408 starts working — the auth fix the PR defers to ENT-2060), Execute returns to executeBatched at line 168 without ever attempting a one-shot push, so AnnouncedTargetLimit is 0 for the whole run. Every in-loop 413 that announces 10 GiB is parsed into `parsedLimit`, used for `limit` and `nextSelfImposedBudget`, and then discarded — the relaxed retry can never fire and the fix is inert for those repos. One line (`if parsedLimit > p.AnnouncedTargetLimit { p.AnnouncedTargetLimit = parsedLimit }`) makes the mechanism self-sufficient and removes the landing-order coupling the PR description has to warn about.

findings.short_summary: Batching/RelayMode unset on every failure path
findings.summary: `result.Batching = true` and `result.RelayMode = "bootstrap-batch"` are assigned only at executeBatched's success return, so every failure path returns Batching=false / RelayMode="bootstrap" — falsifying the syncer change's premise that Execute 'populates these before it can fail'.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed batched bootstrap now reaches the caller as `batching=false relay-mode=bootstrap`, i.e. indistinguishable from a failed one-shot bootstrap — the exact route distinction the syncer change was added to expose. Worse, `Result.Lines()` (internal/syncer/syncer.go:221) gates the temp-ref line on `if r.Batching && len(r.TempRefs) > 0`, so the TempRefs the new error-path Result carefully carries out are still never rendered. Fix at the source: set Batching/RelayMode on `result` before the batch loop, next to `result.Relay`.

findings.short_summary: Strategy facts discarded by every public caller
findings.summary: The carried-out strategy facts are discarded one layer up by every public entry point, so the diagnosability change has no observable effect on any caller.
findings.failure_scenario: `client.go:73` (`return SyncResult{}, fmt.Errorf("sync: %w", err)`), `client.go:57` (Plan), and `unstable/client.go:150/167/186/200` (Plan/Sync/Replicate/Bootstrap) all replace the Result with a zero value on error; `cmd/git-sync/syncplan.go:81` returns before `printOutput`. So the fleet-wide log query the PR wants ('a failed sync could only report its strategy when it succeeded') still returns nothing after this change — the fix is at the wrong depth: it has to reach the client wrappers, or the syncer has to log the route itself.

findings.short_summary: Retry overrides a measured server cutoff
findings.summary: The retry condition compares the announced limit against `selfImposedBudget` without distinguishing 'the budget we chose' from 'a server cutoff we measured', so it discards empirical evidence that the target cuts below its announced figure.
findings.failure_scenario: A reverse proxy cuts the connection at 4 MiB without announcing a limit; `nextSelfImposedBudget` (line 1224) ratchets selfImposedBudget down to sentBytes = 4 MiB. The next push aborts early at 4 MiB, subdivision bottoms out, and `p.AnnouncedTargetLimit` (10 GiB, parsed from the original one-shot 413) > 4 MiB, so the retry jumps the ceiling from a measured 4 MiB straight to 10 GiB. findings.short_summary: Sentinel unexported, so callers cannot errors.Is it
findings.summary: `ErrCheckpointExceedsTargetLimit` lives in an internal package and is not re-exported from the root `gitsync` package, so the caller the doc comment addresses cannot match on it.
findings.failure_scenario: errors.go establishes the repo's convention: every caller-facing sentinel (ErrTargetRefMoved, ErrNoRefsSelected, ErrSourceEmptyUnverified, ErrTargetEmptyUnverified, ErrSourceEmptyTargetPopulated) is aliased into package `gitsync` with a doc block saying 'Test for it with errors.Is'. mirror-pipeline `cmd/worker/syncer_errors.go:225-263` matches exactly those `gitsync.Err*` values. `entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/strategy/bootstrap` is unimportable from mirror-pipeline, so 'callers can treat that as permanent' is unreachable — the worker would have to string-match the message, which errors.go:20 explicitly warns against. Add the alias plus doc block in errors.go.

findings.short_summary: Doc contradicts impl; O(chain) map rebuilt per failure
findings.summary: isIndivisibleCheckpoint's doc contradicts its implementation and it rebuilds a full chain-index map to answer a question that is one subtraction; the `len(batch.chain) == 0` disjunct at line 686 is also dead.
findings.failure_scenario: The comment says it 'reports whether the checkpoint at idx covers a single commit', but subdivideCheckpoints splits every remaining gap, so it returns true only when the entire remaining tail is one-commit-per-gap — a 1-commit checkpoint at idx followed by a 20-commit gap answers false. That makes the sentinel's firing condition depend on unrelated later checkpoints, amplifying finding 1's unpredictability. The intended answer is `chainPosition(chain, batch.Checkpoints[idx]) - chainPosition(chain, current) == 1`, which is correct by construction and avoids allocating a `map[plumbing.Hash]int` over the whole chain (~1M inserts for a linux-sized repo) on every push failure. Separately, `len(batch.chain) == 0` at 686 can never change the outcome — isIndivisibleCheckpoint already returns false for an empty chain.

findings.short_summary: New tests share one shape; miss leak and projection path
findings.summary: All three new tests share one shape — a single branch, a 1-commit chain, and a budget far below minBytesBeforeAbort — so none of them can catch the budget leak, the multi-branch regression, or the projection-based abort that production actually hits.
findings.failure_scenario: Budgets are 64, 256 and 1<<20 bytes while `minBytesBeforeAbort` is 8 MiB (line 1136), so only the absolute `bytesSent >= threshold` branch of shouldAbortPush ever fires — never the projection path that produced the production log line the PR quotes. findings.short_summary: Error-path Result drops Plans, Pushed, Warned, Measurement
findings.summary: The error-path Result is asymmetric with the success path: it drops Plans, Pushed, Warned and Measurement even though bResult.Plans is populated before anything in Execute can fail.
findings.failure_scenario: Execute sets `result.Plans = plans` at line 164, before any failure is possible — the same argument the new comment makes for Relay/RelayMode — yet the error branch omits it, so `fromSyncResult` (results.go:186) yields `Refs: []` and `Measurement: {}` for a failed bootstrap while the success branch at 1421 carries both. findings.short_summary: Relaxed retry re-fetches the whole multi-GiB pack
findings.summary: The relaxed retry `continue`s back through packReaderForCheckpoint, re-fetching the entire indivisible pack from the source rather than reusing the stream it just uploaded.
findings.failure_scenario: For the case this branch exists to serve — one commit whose pack is several GiB — the retry doubles source egress and wall time before the target gets a verdict. Unavoidable without buffering, but worth stating in the comment alongside the 'bounds the waste' rationale, since the retry is the one place in the batch loop that knowingly re-pays a multi-GiB fetch.

findings.short_summary: Helper writes the chain twice, relies on hash determinism
findings.summary: bottomOutParams writes the same 1-commit chain twice into two throwaway stores and relies on the hashes matching across calls; its packBytes parameter is also 4096 at all three call sites.
findings.failure_scenario: `hashes := makeLinearCommitChain(t, 1)` builds one store, then `fetchCommitParents` builds a second `memory.NewStorage()` and calls `writeLinearCommitChain(t, store, 1)` again, so DesiredRefs.SourceHash and the returned parent map only agree because writeLinearCommitChain happens to be deterministic. If that helper ever picks up a real timestamp the three tests fail with an unrelated 'checkpoint not in chain' symptom.
